deeperExplanation.question: Is any self-awareness while speaking a problem?
deeperExplanation.answer: No. A short chosen focus can be useful when learning. The distinction is whether you are exploring one feature or attempting to police everything. You might choose to notice phrase boundaries during a private reading, then let that focus become lighter in conversation. You can also decide that outward attention serves this moment better. The watcher is a description of an experience, not a new thing you must defeat.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Recognise the Watcher. While someone is listening, part of your attention seems to stand beside you. It checks your mouth, predicts the next word and asks whether you look nervous.

In this session, we will recognise self-supervision, distinguish chosen focus from inspection, and return attention to the exchange. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: The watcher is our name for this experience of supervising yourself while speaking. It is a pattern of attention, not a separate person inside you. Recognising it gives you a choice about where attention goes next. We are not trying to eliminate awareness; a little awareness can be useful when learning. We are exploring the difference between a chosen practice focus and a running inspection.

sections.narration:
While someone is listening, part of your attention seems to stand beside you. It checks your mouth, predicts the next word and asks whether you look nervous.

When you are learning a physical skill, brief attention to one movement can help. But trying to check every movement during a conversation may feel crowded. In this session, choose one moment to notice the watcher, then return to the listener’s message. You do not have to check whether the watcher has disappeared.

sections.narration: Watching for the watcher can become another inspection. Notice briefly, name the pattern if helpful, and return. If you cannot tell where attention is, simply answer the actual question. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: During one conversation, return to one detail the other person has shared. Reflect afterwards rather than continuously tracking yourself. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
